findings.meaning: Dispatch delay, combined write admission/preparation, client call through validation, and full client offered/scheduled elapsed already have distributions and CI. They are not backend queue or backend service measurements.

findings.meaning: p8_load queue_us is harness admission to execute_work start (or pre-service terminal), and service_us is execute_work start through terminal, including harness writer wait, mutation and response checking. writer_wait_us times the harness writer mutex. backend_call events and active/peak counters wrap the entire backend call and observe overlap, without separating production executor admission, DB locks or semantic worker waits. ablation explicitly records client queue and combined service/transport. These older observations are real and useful at their named layer, but do not change the missing production-attribution conclusion.

safe_observer_only_partial_work: Keep the existing five client timing families visible instead of reporting only legacy end-to-end quantiles.

Keep original p8_load harness queue/service, writer wait, backend call events/peak and ablation service_and_transport labels when discussing their own source/run. They do not measure production internal queue, DB lock or worker contention and cannot be transplanted into G275 raw.
Read already-retained IndexReport.build_timing and report its named stage/total boundaries separately. Do not subtract it from client time and call the remainder a queue.
Keep existing discrete query_executor and semantic queue counters and their sample times/limits; do not infer continuous maxima.
For future runs, pass request_id through the existing StdioRPC timing callback to operation rows. Preserve raw wire IDs and every terminal attempt.

minimum_product_work_for_full_attributio.change: Add optional bounded in-memory request/operation observation context. Time semaphore wait, blocking submission-to-start, and actual work-to-exit separately. Propagate context across await and spawn_blocking; late work owns its completion recording just as it owns permits. Existing completed/rejected counter semantics, cancellation, deadline, and permit lifetime remain unchanged.

Record request dispatch/terminal and build-gate acquisition boundaries using the same optional observation context; publish explicit diagnostic scope and identity. Global before/after counter subtraction under overlapping RPCs cannot provide individual request service time.

Time read-pool lock/checkout and writer-mutex acquisition at the owner. Audit all participating write facades so observed coverage is explicit; keep mutex guards and transaction ordering intact. BEGIN acquisition elapsed includes SQLite work, so label it as such. Replacing SQLite busy_handler is not needed for application-mutex timing and must not be done casually: exact internal busy-sleep timing would require separate instrumentation without changing the existing timeout/retry behavior.

Record scheduler capacity wait, coalesced scheduling, provider admission and actual round duration with runtime incarnation and operation/round identity. Disabled or never-run phases remain unavailable, not zero. Do not make observation writes update semantic epochs or persisted product telemetry.

Collect the new real diagnostics/IDs, validate field chronology and explicit scope, and let the existing Rust statistics owner produce distributions/CI. Do not add a second Python quantile implementation or change old populations, offered denominators, timeouts, workload, or pass thresholds. Coordinate with PR #175 before touching its owned runtime/statistics paths.
